name: CarTrade Tech Ltd
title: CarTrade Tech Ltd - 543333 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: CarTrade Q4 FY26 PAT rose 54% YoY to INR70.8 crore; FY26 PAT INR243 crore (+68%), with management targeting INR1,000 crore profit in 4-5 years.
summary.overview: CarTrade reported a strong Q4 FY26 with consolidated EBITDA up 55% and margin at 35% for the quarter, and FY26 revenue up 22% with EBITDA margin at 33%. Consumer group (CarWale, BikeWale) grew revenue 25% in the quarter and 30% for the year. OLX India total income grew 16% in the quarter, below the ~18% of the prior quarter, which drew repeated analyst questions. Management pointed to new OLX monetisation products (Elite Buyer, Verification, Super Dost) as the next growth driver, but disclosed that these were still insignificant in revenue terms (under 5% of FY26 revenue).

financial_highlights.change: up 54% YoY; first time above INR70 crore in a quarter
about INR300 crore added in FY26
EBITDA +96%, PAT +55% (aided by higher deferred tax provisions)

financial_highlights.value: INR1.7 million listings; about 3 lakh volumes

segments.name: Consumer group (CarWale, BikeWale)
segments.commentary: Revenue +30% for FY26 and +25% in Q4; FY26 EBITDA margin about 38% per analyst, and management said margin will expand in FY27. Revenue split is roughly 70% OEM and 30% dealer.

segments.name: Remarketing (Shriram Automall)
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% in both FY26 and Q4; FY26 margin 28%, PAT +66%. Around 130 auction sites. Value-added and inspection fees are mostly auction-linked; inspection is under 10% of fees.

segments.name: OLX India
segments.commentary: Q4 total income +16% YoY, below the prior quarter's ~18%; FY26 +22%. Margin rose from 23% to 31%. Elite Buyer and Verification contributed under 5% of FY26 revenue. Employee cost up 4% for the year to INR73-75 crore, and total cost up 1%.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no numerical guidance for FY27 revenue, PAT or quarterly growth; it declined to comment on a INR350 crore FY27 PAT figure raised by an analyst.
Long-term goal: take PAT from INR243 crore to about INR1,000 crore (roughly 4x) within 4-5 years.
Consumer group EBITDA margin expected to expand in FY27; management said margins across all businesses will expand in the current year and costs should be broadly stable.

Management expects Elite Buyer and Verification to become significant revenue lines in FY27, with impact visible from Q1 or Q2 FY27; management said April trends were better than other months but gave no quantified figure.
Management expects new cash generation of around INR300 crore per year for 2-3 years; cash return to shareholders is possible in 2-3 years, subject to tax shelter and carry-forward loss rules.
capex_capacity: Shriram Automall: about 130 physical auction sites; the company is building new supply sources, including a trade-in partnership with one OEM for commercial vehicles and a farm equipment push.
Elite Buyer agent suite (matchmaking, pricing, negotiation, condition check) is at various stages of rollout; Super Dost instant-sale tool for dealers launched about 30 days before the call.
Verification product launched in the last weeks of Q4 FY26, about 45 days later than planned.
Financing product for used-vehicle buyers and marketplace dealer financing (on transaction turnover of about INR4,000-5,000 crore) are under development; no timelines given.
demand_pricing: Industry: car industry grew about 20% in April 2026 and steep growth was seen over the prior seven months, helped by GST rate cuts on cars and bikes.
OLX: about 31 million monthly users; CarWale/BikeWale about 50 million; about 2 million monthly used-car buyers and sellers; buyers outnumber sellers six to one.
Dealer pricing described as largely static; growth comes from volume and relevance, with inflationary price increases only.
Traffic: management said traffic grew YoY in Q4, with Q3 seasonally the highest quarter; the company said about 95% of traffic is organic.
Advertising revenue is insignificant: under 5% in CarWale, under 10% at OLX, and nil at Shriram Automall (per management).
Management said the OLX Q4 slowdown reflected two fewer days in the quarter and a later Verification launch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OLX growth slow from about 18% to 15.5-16% QoQ despite guidance of stronger momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to two fewer days in the quarter, typical October-December seasonality, and Verification launching about 45 days later than planned. It said it was more optimistic than last quarter, with no change in outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What share of OLX revenue comes from Elite Buyer and Verification, and how big could it become in three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Elite Buyer and Verification were under 5% of FY26 revenue. Management said they will become significant in FY27 but gave no sizing; it said the revenue could be more than 30-40% over time, with no ceiling.

qa_highlights.question: How has the remarketing mix (repossession vs retail) and value-added fee share changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said institutional (repossession) volumes are not cyclical and both segments should keep growing. Inspection fees are under 10% of revenue; other fees are mostly auction-linked. Financing is a planned new fee line.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI or ChatGPT-style search threaten the traffic and consumer business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said traffic has grown as search has grown, that proprietary data, OEM/dealer integrations and brand give defensibility, and that AI is a net opportunity for the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROE about 10% and what is the plan for the cash of about INR1,244 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash balance is the main reason for the low ROE. Returning cash or M&A is possible in 2-3 years once tax shelters and loss carry-forwards allow; no specific M&A is in view.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan any acquisitions, such as the AutoMall stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is nothing to report on M&A or cash utilisation; it has done three major acquisitions and remains open to strategic deals with synergy value and reasonable valuation.

risks_watch: OLX growth decelerated to about 16% in Q4 from about 18% in Q3, and management has repeatedly pushed monetisation timing out; watch Q1 FY27 OLX growth and Elite Buyer/Verification revenue disclosure.
AI-led search and assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode) could divert traffic or lead to direct dealer dealings; management disputed this but gave no quantified traffic data.
Consumer and remarketing growth relies on auto industry momentum (post-GST cut); management said steep cost pressures were noted across the industry.
Cash of INR1,244 crore and ROE of about 10%: capital allocation (M&A vs returns) remains undecided and tax-constrained for 2-3 years.
Management guidance is largely qualitative; no FY27 revenue or PAT target was given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the financial trajectory and long-term profit goal, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give quantified guidance for FY27 revenue, PAT or OLX growth, and gave no sizing for new products or M&A plans.
key_quotes: Margins have now gone from 9% to 33%.
I don't want to give a guidance but obviously we believe the growth rate will be stronger than what it is today.
If the cash balance didn't exist, the ROE would be much higher.
one of the goals we've set ourselves is to get to approximately INR1,000 crores profit in the next four-five years which is 4X.

adds.what: Shriram Automall new supply sources: trade-in partnership with one OEM for commercial vehicles and farm equipment push (no capacity numbers given)
Elite Buyer agent suite rollout (matchmaking, pricing, negotiation, condition check) at various stages; Verification product launched late Q4 FY26

growth.why: No numerical FY27 revenue guidance; management targets ~INR1,000 crore PAT in 4-5 years (from INR243 crore) and says margins will expand in FY27, backed only by new OLX products (Elite Buyer, Verification, Super Dost) still under 5% of revenue and no quantified April trend, so backing is vague.
